Chart of the Week: Cass Freight Shipments Index, Cass Truckload Linehaul Index – USA SONAR : CFIS.USA, CTLI.USA
The domestic freight market has been on a long-running rollercoaster since the start of the century. The Cass Freight Shipments Index (CFIS) and the Cass Truckload Linehaul Index (CTLI) show how each cycle has differed from the last, and why predicting when each one begins and ends is extremely difficult.
The CFIS includes shipments across truckload, intermodal , LTL and several smaller modes, making it a good representation of total transportation demand over time. Because it is based on invoice data, it runs with a slight lag.
The CTLI measures the base cost of a truckload move, excluding fuel and accessorial charges. That makes it a good gauge of truckload rates without the influence of fuel, and base rates are a better indicator of supply and demand in the truckload market.
Looking at demand (CFIS) and truckload rates (CTLI) over the past 25 years, we can identify several distinct cycles, with one large anomaly in the middle.
Intra-recession era
Starting in 2000, the CFIS captured the early effects of the dot-com collapse and the economic fallout from 9/11 as the economy slipped into recession. Goods demand stayed muted longer than the broader economy did.
2004 was one of the strongest economic years in modern times. Low interest rates following the weak start to the decade fueled a housing boom, helped along by the subprime mortgage market that would cause problems later. Fuel prices became volatile, and real GDP grew about 3.8%. Strong goods demand and limited capacity fueled the rise of freight brokerages as more than a backhaul play for carriers. Brokers adopted new technology that had become far more accessible as the internet matured. This growing connectivity let smaller carriers haul for larger shippers and fueled the growth of owner-operators over the next decade.
In 2008, the housing market collapsed, triggering what became known as the Great Recession, with weakness lingering into 2010. By early 2011, the economy was recovering, and it grew at a slow but steady pace for the next five years.
The great stabilization defines normal
This post-recession period was the most stable of the past 26 years, and it set many people’s expectations of what “normal” looks like in the freight market. The CFIS followed a clear 12-month seasonal pattern, and base rates grew at about 3% a year until 2016.
Energy markets collapsed in late 2015, leading to a mini freight recession through most of 2016 that many participants did not fully recognize until after the fact. Economic growth slowed from roughly 4% in early 2015 to 1.5% a year later, and the industrial economy struggled. Truckload base rates fell about 2% as demand faltered.
By early 2017, capacity had tightened and demand was returning, and the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, signed that December, added further fuel heading into 2018. Rising demand against shrinking capacity produced one of the strongest and longest spot-rate upswings in modern history. Hurricane Harvey and the ELD mandate made conditions even tighter that fall and winter. Many dismissed the period as a “black swan” that would not be repeated.
As with every rapid expansion covered here, contraction followed. The tax cuts gave the economy a temporary “sugar high.” Meanwhile, capacity grew quickly as strong rates attracted new entrants: active trucking authorities rose about 15% from early 2017 to early 2019.
The 2019 freight recession produced what were, at the time, the largest trucking failures of the century, as truckload carrier Celadon and LTL carrier New England Motor Freight shut down. That made the COVID era even more extreme, because capacity had been leaving the market just before demand boomed.
COVID breaks everything
COVID was the freight market’s second black-swan-type event in three years, which undercuts the idea that such events are rare. Government stimulus, enhanced unemployment benefits and the shift to working from home drove an unprecedented goods-demand boom and supply chain shocks. Once again, the overstimulated environment gave way to a downturn: the longest freight recession of the 2000s, lasting from early 2022 through the 2025 holiday season.
We are now approaching a year into a new cycle. The data suggests that putting a timeline on any cycle is a fool’s errand, and this one, like most, is full of nuance. Higher barriers to entry from regulatory pressure, diesel prices and interest rates are just a few of the factors at play. Demand remains relatively weak, which is hard to reconcile with an inflationary market. According to the CTLI, rates were up 10% in September, while volumes rose only 2%.
There are many lessons. The freight market does not operate on an island; it is shaped by outside forces and by every part of the economy. Expecting the 2010–2015 environment to return may be the worst assumption a business can make when planning ahead.
Timing is not the takeaway
History suggests that 12 months is the low end for how long this cycle will last. With demand still near the bottom of its range, any upside economic surprise could extend it by several months. Anyone betting on rates easing quickly in the coming months is also betting on a broader economic slowdown, and the hit to business revenue that comes with it. CFOs, take note.

Fancy, Lifted GMC Sierra Denali HD Rides Classy on Gloss Black Concave Vossen HFX-5 Alloy Wheels
9 photos
Photo: vossen / Instagram
The good folks over at Miami, Florida-based Vossen , a well-known American manufacturer of luxury and performance aftermarket alloy wheels, have gotten their hands on a batch of cool pictures featuring a GMC Sierra Denali HD pickup truck – and it looks pretty spectacular indeed.
General Motors has carefully taken care of the entire full-size pickup truck series this year. Both the regular Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra 1500 , but also the heavy-duty models, of course. There’s no discrimination, which is a good thing – especially for the customers and enthusiasts.
There are numerous examples, actually: GM Defense morphed a Silverado 3500HD into an autonomous logistics truck platform, but also introduced a brand-new Mongoose 8.3-liter Duramax turbo diesel on the heavy-duty models, complete with 555 hp and a mountain-moving torque of 1,230 lb-ft from the all-new V8. With it, the maximum towing capacity for the Silverado HD and Sierra HD now climbs to no less than 38k pounds
Naturally, the prices also rose accordingly: the 2027 Chevy Silverado HD soars by up to $1,500 for various trims, and the competition-killer 8.3L Duramax alone adds $11,400 before any fees. Of course, many people will actually focus on the regular 1500 versions because there are all-new fifth and sixth generations for the Silverado and Sierra, which come with brand-new design inside and out plus the brand-new 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V8s to replace the lower-displacement predecessors.
There’s a lot to fall in love with on the new 1500 trucks, like the fresh user interface inside which continues to support smartphone mirroring and allows Apple CarPlay and Android Auto to get rid of the biggest controversies GM has kicked off on some of its models. Alas, some folks just can’t be bothered with the modern trends – unless they’re on HD models.
So, a fan of the GMC Sierra HD has transformed their ritzy Denali pickup truck into something that looks great both at the farm, around the warehouse, and even at a glamping off-road location. Dressed in a very nice light-grey-blue hue and fitted with both chrome and gloss black plastic elements, the GMC Sierra Denali HD rides lifted on a set of matching and contrasting Gloss Black Vossen HFX-5 concave alloy wheels.
The latter start from just $525 each in the six-lug configuration, which is available with 17 through 24-inch diameters and 8.5 to 12-inch widths. However, this is the sturdier eight-lug configuration, which starts from $899 for each wheel and ranges from 22 to 24 inches in diameter and from 10 to 12 inches in width. Naturally, the GMC Sierra Denali HD may be quite ritzy in this presentation, but it never forgets that it also belongs on the off-road trails; thus it comes shod with massive all-terrain tires. The Land Yacht Is an Elegant Yet Roam-Ready Camper Van With a Nautical-Inspired Interior Design
17 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Activan
The marine and camper van industry have some similarities regarding how the vehicles are built and the design behind them. You can arguably call a camper van a "land yacht" – that's the name of the camper van I'd like to share with you today, given by its creator.
What we have here is a project based on an AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It's the latest creation made by Activan, a Reno, Nevada-based company specializing in roam-ready Sprinter camper vans.
As usual, let's first take a look at the exterior. This camper van, like all others by Activan, is designed to handle off-roading – and you can tell that as soon as you lay eyes on it.
For starters, it rides on Black Rhino wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. The company also installed an Agile Offroad RIP suspension kit that comes with upgraded shocks, rear leaf springs, and more.
At the rear, you'll come across an Owl Vans B2 carrier with a Monster 40 cargo box. A lot of specialized converters install flares on premium Sprinter-based camper vans – you'll also notice them on this rig.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Activan Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's Vanspeed capsules are paint matched to the van's body and come with half-slider windows.
The most significant exterior mod is on top of the van: a Super Pacific Cloud Cap tent. It has a solid, weatherproof construction with a T-Slot frame and a marine-grade canvas, as well as three zipped windows and a decently sized mattress that can accommodate two people. What's more, its frame holds a Fiamma F45S awning and a front-facing LED light bar.
The rugged exterior look morphs into a luxurious, comfortable interior design. It has a nautical theme, hence the Land Yacht name.
You'll be greeted by a superb mix of holly and teak wood flooring (like you'd see in some yachts ), white shiplap walls, navy blue laminated cabinetry, and a slatted cherry wood ceiling. The look is complemented by a butcher block countertop with a custom stain and gold accents, such as the cabinet or drawer handles.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Activan You'll notice that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the two seats in the cabin are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van.
Two additional seating options are available straight ahead as you enter the van. Activan added two captain's chairs, complete with swivel bases and armrests.
Above, you'll discover two overhead cabinets and the pass-through that leads into the Cloud Cap rooftop tent. To get to the pass-through, you'll need to use a telescoping ladder.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units, one on each side. It features a deep black stainless steel sink with a pull-out tap, a single-burner induction stovetop, a massive residential-size fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a multi-function oven.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Activan A large overhead cabinet with a "floating" magnetic spice rack underneath, six drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter hides an 11-gallon (41-liter) greywater tank for the sink.
A bathroom sits on the driver's side, hidden behind a large conventional door – it's relatively spacious, measuring 36 inches (91 centimeters) in length. The bathroom offers a shower with a handheld wand and a Laveo dry-flush toilet. There's also an L-Track up top that you can use to attach hooks and hang items to dry or store.
Not only is the bathroom practical, but it also looks beautiful. It has matte marble finished walls paired with a gold shower fixture and a teak mat.
Like in most camper vans, the rear part of the interior is taken up by a fixed bed arrangement. It has a queen-size bed with a memory foam mattress, two overhead cabinets, and a ceiling A/C unit.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Activan Underneath the bed, Activan devised a garage that's accessible from both inside and outside the van. It offers abundant storage space in the middle, while its sides are occupied by two tall boxes that accommodate the utility systems.
Power is on the right side – the electrical system's highlights are a 300 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. The company can add batteries for a total maximum capacity of 1,000 Ah.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 42-gallon (159-liter) freshwater tank, a 20-gallon (76-liter) greywater tank mounted underneath the vehicle, and an outdoor shower with a quick connect.
All in all, the Land Yacht by Activan blends fine aesthetics with much-needed practicality. It can be the ideal adventure machine, especially if you want to go off-grid and roam for longer periods.

He Bought a 1976 Chevy Camaro Like He Had in High-School: No Brakes and the Worst Air Cleaner
19 photos
Photo: Royalty Auto Service | YouTube
For this guy, this is a project of nostalgia. It may not be the best car in the world, and definitely not the prettiest. Besides, it has, he says, the "worst air cleaner on the face of the planet Earth." However, he has been dreaming of buying one just like it since the moment he sold it.
Sometimes, just sometimes, nostalgia wins out, and a car guy makes emotional purchases, even though, rationally, it's a bad idea. Sherwood Cooke Jr., owner of a family-run auto repair shop in St. Marys and Kingsland, Georgia, bought a 1 976 Chevrolet Camaro very similar to the one he had when he was in high school, back in the mid-1980s.
The car was his daily driver, even though it was anything but the ideal daily driver. “It would melt your shoe on the floorboard because the headers ran right underneath the driver's side where your foot was,” he recalls.
He had bought that car from someone who had blown the engine after using water instead of coolant in a cold winter, which cracked the block, and he wasn’t going to fix it. Sherwood remembers it as if it were yesterday, but he forgot how much he paid for it. From that moment on, every paycheck he got went into that car.
Photo: Royalty Auto Service | YouTube Sure, it was far from perfect, but it brings back good memories. As for the new one, things got off on the wrong foot. He paid $12,500, even though the original asking price was $10,000. All of a sudden, the seller went straight to $25,000. Sherwood managed to negotiate it down, then load it onto the trailer and drive it to his shop.
He would have gladly driven it home on its own power, because it does run and drive, but it is not exactly drivable. It has no brakes. Sherwood's former boss and mentor, Neal, is going to save the day when it comes to the braking system and to everything else that needs work, for that matter.
He has already started ordering parts for it. He drove it around a bit and says it drives well, as the engine and transmission must have been rebuilt not too long ago. The 350 cubic-inch (5.7-liter) Small-Block V8 engine with a two-barrel carburetor setup sits under the hood.
The V8 was originally rated for a modest 165 horsepower (167 metric horsepower) and 260 pound-feet (353 Newton meters) from the Chevrolet factory. The Camaro was far from a sports car. It took nearly 10 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill and maxed out at 121 mph (195 kph).
Photo: Royalty Auto Service | YouTube However, to stop that non-sports car, he will need a new master cylinder and probably a booster. Neal will know what to do and recommends the buyer stay away from the engine. Sherwood, however, is considering new electric fans. It already has a new electric fuel pump.
The car comes with the steel bumper from the factory, a design choice that wasn’t exactly popular among Camaro enthusiasts. So the new owner is considering painting it to match the red body color. The car is finished in an orange-ish shade of red, but he is planning to change that.
" It definitely won't be pink ," he decides. Peeled paint at the base of the windshield reveals a dark red shade, which might have been the color the Camaro rolled off the production line with back in 1976, and it looks like it sported a color-coordinated cabin.
His car from back in the 1980s was finished in black and had an L88 fiberglass hood, a trend launched with the late-60s Corvette L88s, and it was a race car that he drove on the street. He wants to find a set of Cragar wheels for his new old 1976 Camaro , just like he had on his first car.
Photo: Royalty Auto Service | YouTube The doors are stuck shut, so Neil slides into the cabin through the rolled-down window, fires up the engine, and revs it up before unloading it from the trailer, hooked safely to the winch, because that is all the braking power they’ve got at this point. Back in his teenage years, he wouldn’t have minded it much.
Everything seems to work on board, except for the horn, which seems to have a mind of its own. But there are wires dangling from the upper part of the dashboard, looking like something is missing. The original radio is missing as well, but he eventually finds it wrapped in bubble wrap in the trunk.
He will also have the interior redone. His car used to have a gray interior, but this one came off the production line with seats wrapped in black vinyl. The driver’s seat shows the usual signs of wear and tear. The new owner is also planning a new shifter and aftermarket gauges that show more than the factory ones. Besides, he wants to make it look as much as possible like his old Camaro.
The newly purchased Camaro has no air conditioning, just like Sherwood’s good, old car, but it is equipped with the air cleaner that is " quite possibly the worst air cleaner on the face of the planet Earth ." But it is a love-hate situation. That is the reason he just had to buy the car.
Once he is done with the mechanical part, the new owner is going to send it to the body shop to have it repainted and repair all the dings and dents. Then, it will be the 1980s all over again.

Honda Confirms Wild Civic Type R for the U.S. Market
8 photos
Photo: Honda
Honda is working on a radical version of the Civic Type R with more oomph and looks to match. The concept that previews the production version will debut at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas in November. That is when Honda will announce when the production version is slated to hit the market.
The Honda Civic Type R HRC Concept is finally going from a simple design study into a production reality, specifically tailored for the U.S. market. Following its original global reveal at the 2026 Tokyo Auto Salon, the concept is ready for its North American debut at the 2026 SEMA in Vegas.
The car will integrate HRC motorsport technologies and will be developed based on real-world feedback and expertise from Honda Racing’s professional racing drivers. Rather than just slap a cosmetic upgrade package, Honda will engineer the Civic Type R HRC to deliver a highly refined, track-ready version of Honda's signature "Joy of Driving" directly from the factory.
The production version will be heavily inspired by the track-only TCR race cars, but it is explicitly being developed as a road-legal production vehicle. Considering the violent road behavior of the standard Civic Type R , we'll live to see how the HRC engineers will intentionally mix racing hardware with road-legal restraint.
Photo: Honda They will not strip the Civic Type R solely to break lap records. Instead, they will have to bring high-performance gains that drivers can actually live with. The standard Type R with U.S. spec comes with the high-revving 2.0-liter turbocharged K20C1 inline-four pushing out 315 horsepower (319 metric horsepower) and 310 pound-feet (420 Newton meters) of torque.
The numbers make it the absolute king of power in Honda's U.S. lineup, above what the V6-powered family of Honda-badged SUVs come with from the factory. That is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.9 seconds and max out at 170 mph (274 kph). The setup has to pull 3,188 pounds (1,446 kilograms). The purists’ favorite, a six-speed manual transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
However, Honda is expected to dial up the Civic Type R HRC to produce 335 horsepower (340 metric horsepower). That will be a 20-horsepower increase over the baseline. It may not sound like much, but knowing Honda's way of dialing up cars, it will surely feel like much on the road.
Power gains will come primarily from factory ECU recalibration, a less restrictive intake system, and a custom Akrapoovici/HRC titanium performance exhaust. To sustain hard track abuse while remaining road-going-compliant, the car will borrow hardware from Honda’s Super Taikyu endurance racing program.
Photo: Honda This is expected to bring an upgraded HRC radiator, a much larger front intercooler, and a redesigned front bumper intake to make sure the inline-four won't starve for oxygen. By stuffing more oxygen into the combustion chamber, the engine can cleanly burn more fuel, sustaining its peak 335-horsepower output lap after lap without suffering from power drop-offs.
Honda is reportedly targeting a weight loss between 44 and 66 pounds (20 to 30 kilograms) with the help of extensive use of exterior carbon fiber components. The Civic Type R HRC will most likely ride on lightweight forged aluminum wheels. Lightweight carbon-backed Recaro bucket seats will make their way into the cabin.
The radical version of the Civic Type R will get massive Super GT-inspired wide box fender flares to make room for a wider track and a wider front tire setup for improved front-end grip. A front lip spoiler, a larger rear diffuser, and a taller rear wing with oversized endplates for significant downforce gains will also be part of the plan.
Honda will also upgrade the braking system to match the extra output. Larger rotors and high-performance Brembo six-piston front calipers, most likely painted yellow to confirm its motor racing pedigree, will provide the stopping power.
Photo: Honda Prototypes of the Honda Civic Type R HRC have already hit the Suzuka Circuit. The production-spec car is expected to launch in mid-to-late 2027 as a limited-run 2028 model year. While the standard Type R starts at $47,395 in the United States, before fees and options, the Type R HRC is expected to cost north of $55,000.
The HRC booth at this year's SEMA show in Las Vegas will host an excclusive fleet. The Honda Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck will also be in the spotlight as a ground-breaking desert racer pushing over 1,300 hybrid horsepower from an F1-inspired, 2.4-liter twin-turbocharged V6 setup.
Furthermore, three rugged 2027 Honda Passport TrailSport Baja Chase vehicles, modified with specialized HRC dampers, custom Titan7 forged wheels, and mobile support gear, will keep them company in Vegas.
Rounding out the display are the 2026 Acura ARX-06 GTP Prototype wearing a historic "Thank You" endurance racing legacy livery and coming straight after its win at the 2026 Petit Le Mans at Road Atlanta, and the IMSA Watkins Glen-winning 2026 Honda Civic Type R TCR race car.

2026 SEMA Show • 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition: How Does It Compare to Other Adventure Crossovers?
The Vail 450 FL Is a Luxury but Compact Travel Trailer for Four People
14 photos
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan
Luxury is rarely synonymous with compact dimensions, unless we're talking about jewelry or gadgets, and almost never with RVs. This travel trailer you've never heard of wants to be the exception, if you'll let it – and read the fine print beforehand.
This is the Vail 450 FL, described as "a luxury caravan equipped with premium comfort and top-tier features."
Returning to the question of what luxury is or isn't, it's not always easy to define and delimit. The manufacturer of this caravan wants you to assume that luxury is also relative to whatever else is available in this particular segment right now. It's best to view it from this perspective, if we're keeping it real – and we always are.
This is the largest entry in the Vail series from Turkey-based manufacturer Vail Karavan, an offshoot or spinoff of Serm & Barr, another Turkish specialist with somewhat of a reputation on the European market as well. This floorplan is at the opposite end of the spectrum from the Vail 370 F we checked out earlier this week.
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan While that one is on its way to a European debut, this one isn't, at least not from what I can tell. It launched the company and the Vail series with a local debut in January this year, and it represents a family-friendly solution for campground-bound extended getaways.
What this means is that the 450 FL is only available in Turkey as of this writing, with no announced plans for an international debut. That said, Vail Karavan says all their products are built to European standards and they do ship internationally, so the only thing standing between you and this floorplan is your willingness to deal with import formalities and the extra expenses.
The rest of us can admire from afar.
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan The Vail 450 FL doesn't try to reinvent the wheel in terms of European-standard layout or construction methods, but they do tweak just about everything else around it. The premium galvanized chassis they import from Germany comes with laser-cut holes for weight reduction and a single braked axle with a maximum capacity of 1,350 kg (2,976 kg).
Empty weight on this floorplan, with all the basic features included, is 1,090 kg (2,403 lbs), so you still have a considerable payload capacity to work with.
Total length is 6 meters (19.6 feet), with the body measuring 4.5 meters (14.7 feet) in length and 2.18 meters (7.1 feet) in width. Construction of the body is with vacuum-bonded sandwich panels, thick insulation and an Euramax aluminum outer skin with a hammer-style effect and a seamless fiberglass roof.
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan Vail uses imported double-glazed opening windows , an imported caravan door, and marine-grade flooring and cabinetry for the interior, offering a travel trailer that's designed to last for years of use – and enjoyment. Premium corner supports are included.
The layout won't strike you as particularly innovative especially if you're familiar with European caravans. You have a booth dinette at the front, an L-shaped galley kitchen in the middle, and a French bed at the back, tucked into the rear corner on the off-side. In the opposite corner, you'll find a compact wet bathroom with a vanity right outside.
Vail says that this floorplan can sleep four people, including on the convertible dinette at the front, but that can only be accurate if two of those four people are kids. The dinette isn't a two-person variant but it doesn't seem large enough to fit four adults around the dinner table. Turned into a bed, it can't possibly accommodate two adults in comfort.
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan The kitchen is offered standard with a three-burner gas cooktop under a glass cover, a separate sink with a cover, a compact compressor fridge under the counter, and plenty of storage and prep space. It's not a gourmet kitchen by any stretch of the imagination, but it will do just fine for quick meals on vacation.
At the back, you have a nice king bed on a premium base with springs and a top-tier mattress, padded headboard, and plenty of storage options all around. Next to the head of the bed is a small cubicle that holds the cassette toilet and the shower, while the vanity with the sink is outside.
This type of arrangement might seem odd at best for readers outside of Europe, but here, it's common in smaller caravans and campervans, where space is at a premium and compromise is a must in order to have some semblance of comfort. Vail is able to do it in a way that doesn't feel that odd or intrusive, which they feel backs up their claim this is a "luxury caravan."
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan Standard features on it include a 205W monocrystalline solar panel on the roof, a 100Ah gel battery, a 20A charge controller, a 5kW diesel heater, and a 100-liter tank (26.4-gallon) for freshwater. There's no gray water tank included, and you get a cassette toilet that comes with its own tank (the cassette).
I couldn't find any mention of a water heater on the official page, and that's probably because this floorplan, like the rest of the caravans of this size, isn't exactly meant for showering. That shower is more of an emergency solution.
Photo: Serm & Barr/Vail Karavan Vail Karavan doesn't list a price for the Vail 540 FL because units can be further customized in terms of looks and fabrics. That said, a unit on the second-hand market in Turke sells for around €23,000-€24,000 ($25,600-$26,700), so take that as a reference point. Digitally Reborn Chevrolet Chevelle Pays Its Virtual Respects to Second-Gen SS Hardtop Sport Coupe
8 photos
Photo: mike.g.concepts / Instagram
Chevrolet activates in the sports car field with the C8 Corvette series, but it’s not a traditional American vehicle anymore: instead of a front-engine rear-wheel drive behemoth in the mid-size or full-size class, it’s a nimble and light mid-engine sports car with ample power behind the seats.
General Motors thinks it has all the bases covered because the C8 has V8 engines from base to flagship, including the Stingray and Grand Sport with the all-new 6.7-liter V8 packing 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque, and then all the way to the ZR1X rocking the 5.5-liter twin-turbo V8 and hybrid power for a combined total of no less than 1,250 hp.
As such, the C8 is now more of a European-style sports car and supercar with the added trait of a big and brawny V8 engine (and electrification sometimes) rather than a classic American pony or muscle car, or even adherent to the traditional Corvette recipe of front engine and RWD. The Ford Mustang remains firmly entrenched in that area, playing both in the pony and muscle car fields with the EcoBoost and the Coyote models but also rocking the supercharged Predator V8 for the Dark Horse SC and GTD models.
Stellantis, meanwhile, botched things up for the eighth generation Dodge Charger by launching the EV model first, which didn’t sell well, and arriving late at the party with the Hurricane inline-six for the Sixpack and Super Bee models. Also, there’s no Hemi V8 model or a Hellcat, leaving an exploitable gap in the area of traditional American muscle cars.
No worries, as someone has now come up with a solution for GM to take over the field – a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI in a bid to bring back a legendary Chevrolet nameplate. More precisely, Mike G., the leader of the ' mike.g.concepts ' design studio, "fueled by adrenaline and innovation," has reworked the defunct Chevelle into a modern hardtop coupe.
The iconic Chevrolet Chevelle mid-sizer was extra-famous for its Super Sport versions, and the coupe body style, and especially the second-generation SS models remain enshrined into automotive culture for their combination of looks, elegance, and performance. Now, this unofficial, hypothetical design project is obviously a tribute to the second-gen SS models, given the hardtop body style and the double round headlights or the small rear lights.
But it’s also a contemporary revival of the Chevy Chevelle nameplate, playing all the modern tropes with a muscular mid-size allure: “a sleek, next-generation coupe concept designed to recapture Chevy’s former glory,” according to the virtual artist. He adds that “true to the spirit of the ‘Heartbeat of America,’ I want this car to be powered by a breathtaking, supercharged V8 engine that seamlessly blends retro muscle car heritage with modern aggression.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mike G. 2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
BMW's All-New 2028 X5 M Loses All Camouflage, Albeit Only Digitally – Do You Like What You See?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
There is an entirely new X5 in BMW’s portfolio. The G65-generation, or the G78 (LWB) if you live in China, was unveiled earlier this year, and has been in production at the Spartanburg factory in South Carolina, USA, since August 2026, as well as in the People’s Republic when it comes to the long wheelbase version.
Chance are you are already familiar with it, both inside and out, because this is where the most changes occur. After all, the model features a vizor-like face that is part of the Neue Klasse design language, with tiny kidney grilles, and X-shaped daytime running lights integrated into the headlights. The front bumper is on the aggressive side of things, the back end features wide taillights, a new tailgate that does not have a split-opening design anymore, and a sporty bumper.
There is basically no visible line now between the interior of the new-gen BMW X5 and that of other Neue Klasse models made by the company, including the new 3 Series, i3, and iX3, among others, because they are pretty much the same. And you can blame it on the Panoramic iDrive pillar-to-pillar screen at the bottom of the windscreen, as well as the quirky-looking steering wheel, and the new free-standing infotainment display. There is also an optional passenger screen available for the X5, in case you forgot.
Now, the latest BMW X5 is definitely on the controversial side of things when it comes to the design both inside and out, and the upcoming X5 M will follow in its footsteps. After all, it is this model that will sit at the very top of the family, and word on the street is that it might hit the assembly line in 2028, joined by the first-ever battery-electric X5 M (iX5 M).
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik BMW’s all-new X5 M has already been scooped testing in the open on a few occasions, and some of those prototypes have been used as blank canvased by the pixel-altering crowd in order to preview the model’s exterior design. Speaking of renderings, out latest CGI encounter with this model came from @kelsonik on Instagram, and you can check it out in the gallery above.
The model sports a purple paint finish on the outside, joined by some dry carbon elements, like the skirts on the lower parts of the body, including the front apron that has integrated blades on the sides, the rear diffuser, and the side skirts. The headlights are a bit slimmer this time around, and they retain the X-shaped DRLs.
However, instead of flanking the vizor-like elements, including the tiny kidney grille, they now sit on each side of a larger grille that looks like an evolution of the current one, and features horizontal slats. The front and rear bumpers have been inspired by the M Concept Neue Klasse, the wheels are on the intricate side of things, and we can see that the quad exhaust tips stick out from cutouts on each side of the rear diffuser.
The M badge decorates the larger kidney grille and the tailgate, and it would also be found on quite a few elements in the cockpit. Unfortunately, the latter hasn’t been envisioned by the quoted pixel master. However, it will be pretty much identical to that of the X5 when it comes to the upcoming BMW X5 M , albeit with dedicated load screens and submenus for the displays, an exclusive steering wheel, front bucket seats, exclusive trim and upholstery, and probably a few other tweaks.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Speaking of the modifications, the model will also sit closer to the ground due to the retuned chassis, and will have uprated brakes. The latter are a necessary asset in order to keep the extra power in check, because while it may look controversial, the new BMW X5 M will still be punchy and very fast.
Chances are it might share its plug-in hybrid V8 powertrain with the M5, and the current one has 717 hp (535 kW /727 ps) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque in total, hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 and 3.5 seconds for the M5 Sedan and M5 Touring, respectively. It is yet unknown whether the facelifted M5 will offer more oomph or not, but it is currently in the making, and will enter the Neue Klasse realm with a familiar design and a tech-filled cockpit.
Now, we are not entirely convinced that the 2028 (or is that the 2029?) BMW X5 M will look like the one rendered here by the quoted pixel artist, but to be honest, we wouldn’t be mad at all if it did. Or I wouldn’t, because the exterior design is definitely not bad at all. Well, at least not when compared to other BMW Neue Klasse models. But do you like it? Dad Has Kept This 1984 Chrysler LeBaron Parked for 18 Years, Wants To Pass It On to His Girl
21 photos
Photo: Detail Dane | YouTube
A car enthusiast has been keeping this 1984 Chrysler LeBaron locked in a garage years after years, just making sure that it runs and drives. He wants to preserve the car because one day, he wants to pass it on to his daughter. At the age of eight, she can already see herself driving to high school in her dad's LeBaron.
Brian has had this 1984 Chrysler LeBaron for 18 years. And all of this time, it stayed parked in the family garage, collecting dust instead of miles. When he brought the car home back in 2006, it was already used to sitting. That was exactly what it did before he purchased it: it spent 13 long years in another garage.
However, the time has come for it to hit the road again. Brian wants to prepare it for his daughter, even though she won’t be driving it anytime soon. Brian's daughter is just eight and loves the car that talks to her. It may sound very 2026-ish, but that is exactly what the LeBaron did back in 1984.
The car was equipped with the Electronic Voice Alert (EVA) system, which was Chrysler's most daring step into the 1980s space-age technology. Rather than using a simple beep or buzz, the LeBaron featured a speech synthesizer chip that made the car capable of literally talking to the driver.
Photo: Detail Dane | YouTube Sure, it was a robotic voice, but it was something other cars did not have at the time. That was long before cars told us jokes when you asked them, set the navigation to restaurants when we told them we’re hungry, or adjusted the temperature in the cabin when we let them know we’re cold.
The EVA did not say much, but it could warn the driver in an authoritative male voice, using short sentences such as " Your parking brake is on" or " A door is ajar ." However, it was a love-hate situation. For instance, if a sensor failed or a door switch got loose, the car would repeatedly cycle through warnings. Drivers grew tired of being told " A door is ajar " when driving down bumpy roads.
However, the LeBaron was the right car at the right time in an era when Chrysler needed affordable models to sell more and stay afloat in a challenging market. It was regarded as the car that made the modern front-wheel-drive convertible popular.
It came with the so-called "waterfall" grille, sporting the pattern with closely spaced, thin vertical chrome blades, opera windows on the four-door sedan and the two-door coupe. In the meantime, the convertible rolled off the production line with a folding fabric top with a rear window, upgraded from plastic to glass for the 1984 model year.
{fullimg6]
Built on Lee Iacocca’s famous K-car platform, the 1984 LeBaron also debuted the multi-point electronic fuel injection in the 2.2-liter turbocharged inline-four, which produced 140 horsepower (143 metric horsepower). The 2.2 sat at the top of the lineup.
In the meantime, the base engine was the 2.2-liter inline-four with 96 horsepower (98 metric horsepower), while the 2.6-liter Mitsubishi G54B four-cylinder produced 99 horsepower (101 metric horsepower) under the hood of the LeBaron. Buyers could go for either the five-speed Getrag manual or the three-speed automatic TorqueFlite transmission, as Brian’s car has.
Brian bought it from a friend in Glen Arbor, Michigan. The owner was Elizabeth Weaver, former Chief Justice of the Court from 1999 to 2001. She had kept it in a garage for 13 years. She stopped driving it at some point because the convertible top no longer worked. Besides, she had another little convertible that she used to drive around.
At the time, Brian was in bad need of a car, and she promised she would make a deal with him if he could fix the Chrysler. And he could. But he drove it home and parked it, planning to work on it. However, life happened, and the LeBaron has been sitting ever since.
Photo: Detail Dane | YouTube Now, he called a detailer because he wants to get it cleaned. One day, it will be his daughter’s daily driver, but that day is still very far away. His daughter is just eight. Dane of Detail Dan e loads the car onto his trailer and takes it to his studio for a makeover.
Dust and grime have gathered on the dashboard plastic, and the silver vinyl that covers the seats and door panel on board the LeBaron. So the detailing expert uses the steamer, a degreaser, microfiber towels and brushes to access all the areas and remove the dirt.
He meticulously washes the engine bay, then covers the entire body in foam to decontaminate the paint and get rid of the dust this car has collected over the years instead of collecting miles. He rubs every inch of it to agitate the dirt embedded in the paint finish and in the vinyl convertible top.
The single-stage paint, which Chrysler called Gunmetal Blue, paint code CC6, one of the most popular paint choices at the time, has completely lost its shine and has gone matte. So the only way back to its shine is polishing it.
Photo: Detail Dane | YouTube When Brian walks into the garage, he can hardly believe his eyes. " It looks like it’s on the showroom floor ," he says. His eight-year-old daughter gets in the driver’s seat. She hardly reaches the pedals, but she will be ready for the Chrysler when she is in high school.

The 6 Quirkiest Non-Mercedes Cars Powered by the Same Mercedes-Benz V8
56 photos
Photo: Roos Engineering
Traditionally speaking, some say that Mercedes-Benz is not quite at BMW's level when it comes to making great engines, but the truth is that both German carmakers have built their fair share of legendary powertrains.
Regarding V8s, for example, some would say that the three-pointed star is well ahead of its rival from Bavaria. An example as good as any would be the M117, which not a few would regard as one of the greatest V8 engines of the twentieth century.
Introduced for the first time in 1971, on the 280 SE 4.5 (W108) and 280 SEL 4.5 (W109), it was originally developed to satisfy power demands in the United States. The first version was essentially a longer-stroke sibling to the M116 V8 engine, albeit it gradually increased even further in displacement. Its cast iron block was pretty much unbreakable, and despite the OHC design and only two valves per cylinder, it could be made to deliver quite a lot of oomph without too many reinforcements.
In production for over three decades, it was the top-of-the-range Mercedes-Benz engine until the even more impressive M120 V12 arrived to rewrite all the rules in the early 1990s, but that is a story for another time. Meanwhile, the M117 V8 was modified in so many ways that it powered everything from the S-Class to the incredible G 600 TE AMG that Clay Regazzoni drove in four Paris-Dakar editions despite being paralyzed from the waist down.
The odd part is that this was not a high-tech V8, as its architecture was quite traditional, especially for a German engine, but the combination between its reliability and propensity for large amounts of power with very few modifications made it a great basis for some truly legendary powertrains. For example, the twin-turbocharged M119 V8 that powered the Sauber C8 and C9 at Le Mans used the unmodified M117 block for reliability.
Like other successful and reliable engines, its qualities caught the attention of other, let’s say “boutique” carmakers instead of “less successful ones”. In fact, the M117’s aura is so great that it could be seen as single-handedly responsible for the birth of an automotive brand, not to mention powering some of the most bizarre and less-known supercars. With that in mind, I decided to compile a short list of some of the most obscure cars that were ever powered by the legendary M117, and the interesting stories behind them, especially since none of them was ever sold by a Mercedes dealership.
Isdera Erator GTE Mk III: A Rolling Job Application For Porsche That Started an Enigmatic Legend There aren’t many cars in history that can claim to have been used as literal CV, apart from indirectly being the launch pad for a boutique supercar manufacturer. The third iteration of the Isdera Erator GTE is simultaneously both of those things, and the story behind it could be very well made into a movie.
Eberhard Schulz was a young mechanical engineering student in late 1960s Germany who left his studies before completing his degree in order to follow his lifelong dream of designing the coolest and also most bizarre cars in Germany. Using his laundry room and front yard for space, he designed and built a Ford GT40-like sports car that gradually became a supercar.
Photo: Carola Daimler Named after the first name of his wife, the two-seater mid-engine coupe was based on a welded steel tube frame with a fiberglass body on top, and featured gullwing doors, thus making it not quite identical to a GT40. The Erator GTE underwent several development stages, ultimately leading to the Mk III version. The original iteration had a tiny flat-four Boxer engine from the VW Beetle, which only gave it a top speed of 175 kph (109 mph).
After that, the Mk II was fitted with a much more powerful Cologne V6 engine from the Ford Capri, almost doubling its power and increasing the top speed to over 220 kph (137 mph). The final iteration of the Erator GTE, and arguably the most important one, received a modified brand new V8 developed with racing in mind, and that V8 was based on the now venerable M117. With dry sump lubrication, four open Weber IDA dual carburetors and the displacement increased to 4.9 liters, the Erator GTE Mk III developed a massive 389 PS (384 HP).
I say massive because the model could now reach no less than 315 kph (196 mph), making it faster than the GT40 it harked back and even the contemporary Lamborghini Miura. Schulz then used the Erator GTE Mk III as a rolling job application to try and persuade either Porsche or Mercedes-Benz to give him a job, as he was a fan of both companies. Porsche offered him one in the styling department, where he spent several years in the 1970s developing his design and engineering skills that would eventually lead to the CW311 concept he made for Mercedes-Benz.
That concept eventually became the foundation for the Imperator 108i, another supercar powered by the M117 engine, and the Isdera car company. Amazingly, the Erator GTE Mk III prototype still exists and is currently for sale by a dealership that, even more amazingly, is run by Carola Daimler, who is none other than Gottlieb Daimler’s great-granddaughter.
Monteverdi Tiara: The Swiss W126 S-Class That Wanted to Beat Rolls-Royce But Failed Peter Monteverdi was a Swiss watchmaker’s son and a former racing driver who was originally the national importer for Ferrari in Switzerland. After a falling out with Enzo Ferrari, he surprisingly decided in 1967 that he needed to create his own luxury performance brand This is how Monteverdi the brand was founded, and for about a decade it was among the coolest grand tourer makers of Europe, and the only one in Switzerland.
Almost constantly under the radar, Monteverdi did make a name for itself in the early years with cars like the High Speed 375 Series, which were powered by Chrysler V8s and had bodies styled by none other than Pietro Frua and then by Fissore. That business didn’t really take off, so Monteverdi switched to become a boutique coachbuilder in the late 1970s.
Photo: Isdera The company became relatively famous for the Safari, a luxury SUV based on the American International Scout, and in the early ‘80s it was even responsible for Land Rover making the first-ever 5-door version of the Range Rover, based on a Monteverdi coachbuilding project.
The Tiara was Peter Moneteverdi’s last take on coachbuilding, and it was essentially a slightly retouched Mercedes-Benz S-Class W126 that was supposed to take on Rolls-Royce. Pretty much the entire car was an S-Class, but the front and rear ends were bespoke, as was the interior, while the wheelbase was slightly stretched. Because of the donor body, the Tiara also used S-Class engines, including a 5.0-liter M117 V8 that delivered 231 PS (228 HP), paired with a four-speed automatic transmission also made by Mercedes-Benz.
Partly because it was technically identical to a W126 but probably also because the obvious Peugeot 505 taillights didn’t exactly scream luxury, the dream of dethroning RR collapsed even before the car entered production. Apparently, only three models were ever completed, making it one of the rarest cars ever to feature the M117 mill.
Isdera Imperator 108i: The First Production Supercar With a Periscope As the first production car in history to be initially fitted with a periscope-like rearview mirror as standard equipment, the Imperator 108i was also the second car ever made by Isdera, which is actually an acronym standing for “Ingenieurbüro für Styling, Design und Racing” (Engineering Office for Styling, Design, and Racing). As you already guessed by now, Isdera was founded and run by none other than Eberhard Schulz, who was no stranger to Mercedes or their M117 V8 engine.
As mentioned before, Schulz had developed the CW311 concept in the late 1970s, which had impressed Mercedes-Benz so much that they even allowed it to wear the three-pointed star when it was unveiled at various auto shows. They did, however, decline to put it into production, albeit supporting Eberhard Schulz in developing his first Isdera cars, including the Imperator 108i.
Photo: Isdera Yet another mid-engine supercar with gullwing doors, the Imperator 108i was stylistically based on the CW311, which had been named this way because it represented its drag coefficient. Both cars had the same wedge silhouette, the upward-opening doors and the periscope mirror. Like the Erator GTE, the Imperator 108i was based on a tubular steel spaceframe and had a fiberglass body on top, with its weight being kept under 1,250 kg (2,756 pounds).
Thanks to Eberhard’s connection with Porsche, the model originally used a lot of interior components from the Porsche 928, such as the door handles, all the switchgear and the instrument cluster. In other words, this was not exactly a shed-built supercar but a rather quality offering.
The initial powertrain was a bog-standard 5.0-liter M117, which developed 237 PS (234 HP) and 406 Nm (299 lb-ft) of torque, sent to the rear wheels through a 5-speed manual gearbox. For 1984 this was no slouch, hitting the 100 kph (62 mph) mark in just 5.1 seconds and having a top speed of 283 kph (176 mph). It was definitely much quicker than cars like the Ferrari 208 GTB, for example.
Over its 9-year production run it received numerous upgrades to its M117 engine, culminating with a 6.0-liter AMG version that developed 390 PS (385 HP) and could propel the car to well over 300 kph (186 mph). Despite having so many updates and such a long production run, only 30 examples are believed to have been ever built, each one being customized for its owner.
Lotec C1000: One Thousand Horsepower Before It Was Cool Seriously wealthy people usually live in a different realm compared to regular folks, which is why their dreams are less of a dream and more like a medium to long term plan when it comes to having a car perfectly suited to their tastes. If you have enough moolah you can go to any one of your favorite car manufacturers and simply demand that they make a car specifically for you.
This is exactly what a seriously wealthy citizen of the United Arab Emirates did in the early 1990s, when he contacted Mercedes-Benz with a request that was essentially a very simple, yet a highly demanding brief; he literally wanted them to build him the fastest car in the world. Sadly, or perhaps not, Mercedes politely said no. Instead, they contacted Kurt Lotterschmid, the man behind Lotec.
Photo: RK Motors Lotec was a small but ambitious German company with a rather impressive background of developing Group C racing cars in the 1980s and various bespoke Mercedes, Porsche and even Ferrari models for well-off customers. Long story short, after four years of development with the implication of Mercedes-Benz and over $3 million, Lotec delivered what was arguably the most insane hypercar of the 1990s, which is an odd thing to say when the McLaren F1 was being made at around the same time.
The Lotec C1000 had a claimed top speed of 431 kph (268 mph) long before the Bugatti Veyron officially passed the 400 kph (248 mph) mark, albeit nobody has officially verified it. In case it wasn't obvious from the claimed performance numbers, the “1000” in its name came from the amount of power it developed.
At the heart of the incredible project sat a heavily modified version of the M117 engine, upgraded with a twin-turbocharging system by Lotec, which delivered exactly 1000 PS (987 HP) and 980 Nm (723 lb-ft) of torque. In 1995, those figures would make it the most powerful road car on the planet, with almost 400 horsepower more than the McLaren F1. LEt’s not forget, that power was delivered by an engine whose original design had been introduced in the early 1970s.
Isdera Autobahnkurier AK116i: The Twin-Engined Cruella Car With VW Beetle Parts If the Lotec C1000 is the rarest car to ever sport a Mercedes-Benz M117 engine, while the Monteverdi Tiara was only built in three units, the Isdera Autobahnkurier AK 116i would probably sit somewhere in the middle. I say this because despite being a one-off, it used two M117 engines at the same time.
The work of the same Eberhard Schulz, the bizarre model took almost two decades to be completed, and was never meant to be offered for sale. Its ginormous hood was not only chosen to look spectacular from the profile, but to house two M117 5.0-liter V8 mounted nose-to-nose. Eberhard had long been infatuated with streamlined 1930s cars, and particularly the original Mercedes-Benz Autobahn Kurier models.
Photo: Roos Engineering Essentially one of the first grand tourers, as made evident by its name, the 1930s Mercedes was built in four units, some with a supercharger and some without, and were arguably among the coolest cars with a three-pointed star of their era. Schulz’s twin-engine iteration of the design was started in the 1980s but mechanical and financial issues postponed its official reveal until 2006.
The twin-engine setup also includes two automatic gearboxes made to run in tandem, and thus making the car all-wheel-drive. If the doors look familiar it’s because the actual cockpit is a widened body of a VW Beetle, put on top of a bespoke chassis housing the two engines.
The combined output of the two M117 V8s is around 600 PS (592 HP), and despite weighing as much as a small moon it can hit 242 kph (150 mph). Even more peculiar, the top speed is electronically limited, since Schulz calculated that the fuel consumption at above 250 kph (155 mph) would render the car useless as a grand tourer.

This Custom Camper Van Shows a Short Wheelbase Van Can Still Be a Proper Home on Wheels
21 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans
Someone who's not familiar with camper vans might look at one and wonder how people can travel long-term in them. Well, with a clever design like the one I'd like to share with you today, you can turn even a small van like the Sprinter 144" into a full-time home on wheels.
What we have here is a project based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 2500 with a 144" wheelbase. It was brought to life by Custom Crafted Vans, a Boise, Idaho-based company specializing in high-end, bespoke mobile homes. This is its 60th creation.
Custom Crafted Vans does truly premium camper van conversions. It shared that this was more of a budget build to them, with a simpler interior setup and not that many exterior upgrades . It might be a budget build compared to other of the company's projects, but it's definitely not a budget build in an objective way.
As always, let's first take a look at the van's exterior. You can tell this is an adventure-ready home on wheels as soon as you lay eyes on it. First off, it rides on black wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires.
This Sprinter van came from the factory with a 4-inch lift and an AWD drivetrain - paired with the wheel and tire combo, these make it ideal for going off the beaten path. Custom Crafted Vans improved the off-road capabilities even further by installing a Van Compass Stage 2.3 suspension kit, which comes with adjustable front and rear Falcon shocks. The company also added Opti-Rate leaf springs.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans An Aluminess Legacy ladder on the driver-side offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll discover a large Aluminess rack holding a 410 W solar array, a flat-mounted StarLink antenna, and a Carefree powered awning with an integrated LED light strip.
The solar panels are attached to a raised roof rail, which made it possible for them to sit above a large Dometic CoolAir RTX 2000 A/C unit. Moreover, the rack offers extra space for you to add a cargo box or any other smaller accessory you want.
Other notable mods are running boards, power and water connections, and an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) carrier with a cargo box. Furthermore, the lower rocker panels, bumpers, and grille are coated in black truck bed liner for an extra layer of protection.
The roof is also sprayed with a color-matched truck bed spray that not only protects it, but also prevents rust from forming. This treatment is applied after the roof cut-outs are done.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans Inside is where you can see just how good the company's work is. Enter, and a warm and bright interior will greet you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Moreover, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van and used once you've set up camp.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for Custom Crafted Vans' signature design. It consists of white oak cabinetry, a slatted white oak ceiling, and Roman clay walls. The look is complemented by black accents, like the cabinet and drawer handles, and a Lonseal Lonridge Moccasin-colored floor.
Behind the driver's seat, you'll come across a floor-to-ceiling unit integrating two closets with multiple shelves. You also get additional storage space in a headliner shelf above the cabin that has zipped covers.
Next to it, the company installed a highly sought-after camper van facility: a bathroom. Hidden behind a retractable self-cleaning Nautilus door, it offers a shower with a handheld wand, a portable Laveo dry-flush toilet, and a clothesline.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans The bathroom pairs nicely with the rest of the interior design, as it has large grey Palisade tiled walls and black hardware.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It blocks part of the entrance but leaves enough space for anyone to enter comfortably. It features a deep black stainless steel sink with a pull-out tap, a 65-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a flip-up table for additional counter space.
A portable two-burner induction stove is available for cooking. What's more, a Maxxair vent fan above will draw out the smells and fumes from cooking, and you can use a small cabinet underneath the sink for storage.
When it isn't in motion, most of the time spent in the camper van will be in the back, in the seating and sleeping area. It has a large U-shaped couch made up of three benches, as well as a large swivel table in the middle.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans Setting up the bed is quite quick and simple. You must remove the tabletop, attach it between the long benches on the side to connect them, and do the same thing with an additional panel. The result is a large bed spanning across the van's width. You also get two overhead cabinets on each side and charging points.
The two benches I mentioned hide the rig's utility systems. Power is on the right side – the electrical system's highlights are an 810 Ah lithium battery and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running. If used correctly, you'll struggle to run out of power.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, an outdoor shower connection, and a 2.5-gallon (9-liter) water heater.
One of the overhead cabinets hides the van's "command center." It includes a touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power system, two awning control switches, and other switches for the lights and more.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Custom Crafted Vans There is one more system upgrade worth mentioning. The builders added an AudioControl audio system with two speakers integrated into the rear doors and one above the kitchen.
Despite the limited space, this Sprinter 144-based conversion by Custom Crafted Vans packs quite a number of comforts. It's fit for both shorter escapades and longer off-grid travel, both on and off the road.

Digital 2027 Nissan Z Shooting Brake Comes Packing With a Widebody Kit and Big-Lipped Copper Wheels
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Japanese automaker Nissan has had many novelties for automotive enthusiasts over the past few weeks, including for a few of its most important regions like Australia or North America.
Last month, Mitsubishi announced the pricing of its new Eclipse Sportback, and Nissan dropped laughing because the EV is around $8k more than its Leaf despite the obvious sharing of major hardware. Nissan also had Nismo open its first performance center outside the home market of Japan all the way in the Land Down Under, while Mexico got a taste of the new Frontier Pro with both ICE and plug-in hybrid powertrains, and Nissan announced that its US deliveries have gone up for almost 20 uninterrupted months thanks to carried momentum by the Rogue, Frontier, and the new Armada.
Surprisingly, the automaker also revealed a few weeks ago that its Altima is not biting the dust like other passenger cars for the 2027 model year – though it does cost more, of course. Last but not least, the 2027 Nissan Pathfinder got a retro throwback to its roots from 1987 through new special edition models adding extra comfort creatures.
Anyway, that’s all the news about Nissan from the past month, condensed – and, unfortunately, it doesn’t say anything about the 2027 Nissan Z, the company’s last surviving sports car on the US automotive market. The latest model year is offered both in the US and Canada , where it’s also much cheaper, by the way, with several enhancements, including the addition of a six-speed manual transmission for the Nismo version.
The 2027 Nissan Z also gained some features from the defunct R25 Nissan GT-R to make it even more capable both on the street and at the local track, as well as various subtle changes compared to the previous model years, including a new Shinkai Green Pearl Metallic exterior color which can be combined with the Z Performance’s new tan interior upholstery option to make it vintage cool.
Anyway, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has decided to stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and make it far more enticing with a brand-new body style. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the 2027 Nissan Z with an unofficial, hypothetical Shooting Brake design project.
It’s not just more practical thanks to the added space behind the seats, but it also has a decidedly Japanese flavor thanks to the combination of a striking yellow paint and the gloss black roof mixed with a JDM-style widebody fender flare kit and the new copper-hue big-lipped alloy wheels.
